definitions.meaning: Liquid water turning into invisible water vapour when it is heated, for example by the sun.
Water in its gas form. It is invisible, but it is still water and it is still there in the air.
Water vapour cooling down and turning back into tiny liquid water drops.
Water falling back to the ground, most often as rain, when drops grow too heavy to float.
Fallen water gathering together again in rivers, lakes and the sea.

mechanismSteps: Evaporation: the sun heats liquid water in the sea and in puddles, and the water turns into invisible water vapour that rises into the air.
Condensation: high up the air is cold, so the water vapour cools and turns back into tiny liquid drops, and billions of those drops gathered together form a cloud.
Precipitation: the drops in the cloud join and grow bigger and heavier until gravity pulls them down to the ground as rain.
Collection: the rain gathers in rivers, lakes and the sea, where the sun can heat it again - the cycle starts over and never ends.
objectives: Name the four stages of the water cycle in order: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, collection
Define the key vocabulary of the cycle: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, collection and water vapour
Explain why evaporated water is not gone for good
subject: science
title: The Water Cycle

trap.explanation: This is wrong because the water only looks gone: vapour is invisible, so it feels as if the water has vanished. In fact the water is still there in the air as water vapour. It cools into clouds and falls back as rain, so the same water keeps going round the cycle - evaporation changes its form, it never removes it.
trap.misconception: Water disappears for good once it evaporates.

workedExample: Follow one puddle after rain. In the morning the puddle is full of liquid water. The sun heats it and the water evaporates, rising as invisible water vapour - the puddle shrinks, but the water is not gone. High up, the vapour cools and condenses into a cloud. In the afternoon the cloud's drops grow heavy and fall as precipitation, and the water collects in the same puddle again, ready to start the loop once more.
